messages:
lucy: dumping traces from last night's 1f1b run on 8xA100, microbatch=8. seeing repeating latency spikes (~1.5x) every ~2k steps, not correlated with load.
rahul: can you paste the profiling output? flamegraph or nvprof snippet helps.
lucy: pasted top-level nvprof sample: ```AllReduce: 12.3ms | Kernel(fp16_attention_long): 3.1ms | Kernel(fp16_attention_short): 1.2ms | KVCacheLookup: 0.9ms | memcpy H2D: 0.5ms``` spikes show AllReduce jumping to ~35ms during the tail.
zach: that AllReduce jump smells like fragmentation/fusion overhead. are we hitting tiny tensors frequently? microbatch=8 with 1f1b gives lots of small grad exchanges.
maria: also noticed kernel selector is switching to the "short" attention kernel for ~30% of tokens even though seq_len avg is 1024. Kernel heuristics might be using token-chunking thresholds incorrectly.
lucy: here's the full trace excerpt (condensed): ```[step 4100] forward kernels: attention_short, attention_long toggles; backward: allreduce(grad shard) spikes; timeline shows gap between compute and next forward ~40ms```.
rahul: could be kv-cache memory pressure causing early eviction -> recompute or stalls? any OOM logs or page faults?
lucy: no OOM. but KVCACHE stats show churn: hitrate drops 2% during spikes. seems correlated.
tony: hypothesis: microbatching policy creates many short-seq buckets that pick the short-kernel (cheaper per-token) but increases number of allreduce ops because shard sizes change. small allreduce payloads have higher latency per-byte.
zach: we should try two quick experiments: 1) force kernel selector to prefer long-kernel for seq>256; 2) increase microbatch to 16 to reduce frequency of allreduce calls. both cheap to run on staging.
maria: also test allreduce fusion: bump `collective_fusion_bytes` from 4MB to 8MB in scheduler, that should reduce small RPCs.
lucy: running experiment A now (kernel hint). job: `ci/pp-kernelhint-2058`.
infra-bot: ci/pp-kernelhint-2058 started on pool/gpu-8-a100. logs: https://ci.internal/2058
lucy: short update: kernel hint removed the attention_short toggles -> more consistent kernel runtime, but allreduce still spikes albeit less frequently. hitrate stabilized.
rahul: good. next try microbatch=16 + fusion=8MB. that should both increase per-allreduce payload and decrease interleaving.
lucy: started experiment B: `ci/pp-mb16-fusion-2058`.
lucy: quick numbers after 10k steps (compared to baseline): tail latency 18% -> 9% reduction, AllReduce 95th from 42ms -> 18ms, token throughput +6%.
zach: promising. any regression in sample quality or memory headroom?
lucy: memory used +6% but still within Dedicated pool. no quality diffs on smoke evals.
maria: long-term we should update batching heuristics: group microbatches by seq_len bucket earlier (kernel affinity) and apply a sliding fusion window for allreduce. also add KV cache pressure metric to alerting so we can catch churn.
rahul: agree. action items:
- lucy: run a 48-hour A/B on staging comparing baseline vs mb16+fusion (job queued)
- tony: PR for kernel selector tweak with a config flag and unit tests
- zach: add metric `kvcache.churn_ratio` and alert if >0.01 sustained
- maria: draft note for runbook (how to mitigate tail spikes: mb tuning, fusion, kernel-hints)
lucy: added checklist to the job and pushed initial traces to: https://perf.internal/pp/2058
tony: I'll own the kernel selector PR, aiming EOD.
rahul: thanks all. huge improvement already. let's not forget to run long-run stability (1f1b can reveal slow degenerations).
maria: nice work team :rocket:
lucy: will post final summary + perf graphs when the 48h A/B completes.
infra-bot: ci/pp-mb16-fusion-2058 completed: success. artifacts at https://ci.internal/2058/artifacts
